# PEN-4990 — assert WHICH containers receive the github.com credential

PR: [#3103](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/3103)

## Files

- `src/server/job-manifest.github-credential-container-set.test.ts` (new)

## What changed

A test only. No production source under this adapter is touched.

The sibling of the file of the same name added to the claude_k8s adapter in the
same PR. It walks every container in the assembled pod spec and pins an exact
map of container to the github.com credential routes it receives — the Secret
volume mount (matched by both mount path and Secret name, and counting an
ancestor mount as reaching the credential) and the env route.

## Why

PEN-3183 §7.2 trigger 3 — "any change that widens read access to the token
Secret, or mounts it into a new container" — had no assertion over the set of
containers receiving the token. `opencode_k8s` is a registered
external-lifecycle adapter type (`packages/shared/src/validators/agent.ts`) with
its own `buildJobManifest` and the same Secret propagation, so asserting this
only for claude_k8s would answer "which containers hold the credential in an
agent Job" for one of the two builders that render one.

Two differences from the claude_k8s sibling, both reflected in the
expectations rather than papered over:

- there is no publish broker here, so there is one arrangement, and the
  credential is the agent container's;
- the agent inheritance allowlist is applied at BUILD time inside the
  propagation loop rather than at capture time, so the fixture feeds a
  non-allowlisted credential-shaped Secret and asserts it reaches no container.
  Verified by mutation: adding that Secret to the allowlist reds the file.

The test is DIRECTION-BLIND and says so in its own header: it reds on a
credential route being removed exactly as on one being added.

## Review round 2 (#3103)

Review found the route predicate too narrow. Added a `secretRefs` bucket that
matches the referenced SECRET rather than the env variable name, and folded
`projected` volume sources into the volume->Secret map, so a credential bound
by `env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef`, by `envFrom[].secretRef`, or carried by a
projected volume at a non-credential path is no longer a green.

Exercising that path turned up a genuine difference from the claude_k8s
adapter, now asserted on both sides rather than assumed: THIS adapter
re-applies `isAgentInheritableEnvName` (and `isAgentInheritableEnvFromRef`) at
BUILD time, in the `inheritedEnvValueFrom` loop and the `envFrom` filter, where
claude_k8s trusts the capture-time filter and emits what it is given.

The new case asserts both halves, because asserting only the dropped one would
pass with the detector deleted:

- `MY_TOKEN` bound to `paperclip-github-mcp-token` is DROPPED by the build-time
  name filter — recorded as current behaviour, and deliberately not relied on
  as the boundary: it filters env NAMES and says nothing about which Secret is
  referenced;
- `ANTHROPIC_GH` bound to the same Secret PASSES, because it matches the
  `ANTHROPIC_` allowed prefix, and is reported by the bucket. That is the route
  that actually reaches the agent container.

## Review round 3 (#3103)

Review noted `CREDENTIAL_SECRET_RE` was anchored on a `token` SUFFIX, so a
credential Secret renamed to e.g. `paperclip-github-pat` was invisible to the
Secret-name half and to the `secretRefs` bucket. Non-blocking, and review
offered either loosening the regex or noting it as declared surface.

Did neither exactly. A blanket loosen would swallow `paperclip-github-app-creds`
— the control-plane credential this file deliberately keeps out of scope — and a
header note would leave the fail-open standing in the one place with no
fallback: a `secretKeyRef` names no path, so the Secret name is the only signal
`secretRefs` has.

Instead the matcher is now `isCredentialSecretName`, which FAILS CLOSED: the
whole `paperclip-github-*` family is credential-bearing by default and the
exceptions are enumerated: exactly `paperclip-github-app-creds` and
`paperclip-github-webhook-secret`, both control-plane, both live `secretKeyRef`
targets in the StatefulSet, and both covered by the server-only inheritance
allowlist instead. A new Secret in that family is treated as a credential until
someone decides otherwise: a false positive is a red a human reads, a false
negative is silence.

A third exception, `paperclip-github-app-key`, was dropped on #3103: no Secret
by that name exists anywhere, so it excluded nothing today and pre-approved a
hole tomorrow. Mutation-confirmed — a Secret of that name mounted into a
container at a non-credential path reds with the entry gone and is invisible
(5/5 green) with it present. An exclusion must name a Secret that ACTUALLY
EXISTS and be held out by that different control; the test headers now carry
that rule.

Verified by mutation: restoring the suffix-anchored regex reds the matcher test.
